title: 哈姆雷特 3-3 祈禱中的國王
style_suffix: black and white ink comic style, high contrast, heavy shadows, cold gothic atmosphere
characters: King Claudius, a broad heavyset king with a neatly trimmed dark pointed beard, a wide gold crown, fur-trimmed brocade robes, a jeweled goblet in hand

panels.prompt: {characters} handing a sealed commission to Rosencrantz, a plump smooth-faced courtier with a short blond bowl-cut and an eager ingratiating smile, and Guildenstern, a thin courtier with lank dark hair and nervous darting eyes, in a candlelit council chamber, his smile gone entirely

dialogue.speaker: 克勞地
dialogue.text: 我不喜歡他現在的樣子。你們兩個護送他去英格蘭——國事不容我坐視這樣的瘋狂逼近。
dialogue.en: I like him not, nor stands it safe with us to let his madness range... I your commission will forthwith dispatch, and he to England shall along with you.

panels.prompt: close shot of two heavy ringed hands slowly setting the wide gold crown down on the council table beside a guttering candle, the king's face out of frame above, the crown's shadow stretching long across the scattered papers

dialogue.speaker: 克勞地
dialogue.text: 啊，我的罪惡的戾氣已經上達於天。一個兄弟的謀殺——人類最初、最古老的詛咒，就壓在它上面。
dialogue.en: O, my offence is rank, it smells to heaven; it hath the primal eldest curse upon't, a brother's murder.

panels.prompt: from behind, the heavyset king kneeling in his fur-trimmed robes before a small private altar with two candles, head bowed out of sight, the discarded gold crown lying on the flagstones beside him, his shadow swallowing the altar steps

dialogue.speaker: 克勞地
dialogue.text: 我能夠祈禱嗎？我的手裡還握著那些引我犯罪的東西——我的王冠、我的野心、我的王后。抓著贓物的人，懺悔有什麼用？
dialogue.en: But, O, what form of prayer can serve my turn? 'Forgive me my foul murder'? That cannot be; since I am still possess'd of those effects for which I did the murder, my crown, mine own ambition and my queen.

panels.prompt: behind the kneeling king, a chapel doorway in deep shadow, Hamlet, a lean young prince dressed head to toe in black, a short dark cloak, tousled dark hair, pale clean-shaven face with shadowed sleepless eyes, frozen mid-step with his sword half drawn, candlelight on the bare steel

dialogue.speaker: 哈姆雷特
dialogue.text: （低聲）他在祈禱。我現在動手，正是時候——
dialogue.en: Now might I do it pat, now he is praying; and now I'll do't.

panels.prompt: close-up of the half-drawn sword sliding slowly back into its sheath, the black-clad prince's pale face above it twisted between hatred and calculation, the kneeling king a blur of candlelight beyond

dialogue.speaker: 哈姆雷特
dialogue.text: 慢著。他在懺悔的時候被殺，靈魂會乾乾淨淨地上天堂——這是報仇嗎？不。收起來，我的劍；等一個更可怕的時機。
dialogue.en: And so he goes to heaven; and so am I revenged. That would be scann'd... Up, sword; and know thou a more horrid hent.

quote.text: 收起來，我的劍；等一個更可怕的時機
quote.en: Up, sword; and know thou a more horrid hent.

panels.prompt: the prince slipping away from the chapel doorway into darkness, one last backward glance over his shoulder, the two altar candles tiny in the black

dialogue.speaker: 哈姆雷特
dialogue.text: 我的母親在等我。——這一服藥，不過是替你延長幾天病痛的生命。
dialogue.en: My mother stays: this physic but prolongs thy sickly days.

panels.prompt: the king rising as a heavy black silhouette against the two altar candles, the gold crown dangling from one slack hand, wax pooled and dead on the altar stone

dialogue.speaker: 克勞地
dialogue.text: 我的言語飛上天去，我的思想留在地上。沒有思想的言語，永遠到不了天堂。
dialogue.en: My words fly up, my thoughts remain below: words without thoughts never to heaven go.

quote.text: 言語飛上天去，思想留在地上
quote.en: My words fly up, my thoughts remain below.
